clue.text: God, Olympic finalists are in great terror

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: the finalists of a word are the letters standing at its finish, here the closing pair of Olympic

explanation.surface: Athletes in an Olympic final, overcome by stage fright as a deity looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finalists' here takes the closing pair of letters of Olympic, not just one; the surface's great terror is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is a sudden overwhelming fear, a synonym for great terror.

clue.text: One who goes to bed head first, after natives?

definitions.text: One who goes to bed head first, after natives?

parts.words: One who goes to bed head first, after natives?
parts.note: the bed is the sea bed, plunged into head first, and natives are oysters, bred in beds, sought for what they may contain

explanation.surface: Someone diving into bed headlong, perhaps chasing the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natives' is a British name for oysters (especially Colchester or Whitstable ones), and the 'bed' is an oyster bed on the sea floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver who plunges to oyster beds in search of gems collects natives, the British term for oysters.

clue.text: Cheer-leader, after tricky routine, is disturbed

indicators.note: after places the cheer-leader letter behind the anagram
something tricky is twisted or intricate, so the word routine is rearranged
the leader of Cheer is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cheerleader is rattled after a difficult routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' is the anagram signal on routine; Cheer-leader looks like a person but gives only the opening letter, placed last by 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurotic person is anxious and emotionally unsettled, which is what disturbed means here.

clue.text: Order oxygen for an amphibious soldier

parts.note: to order is to command
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An officer calls for oxygen for a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Commandos are raiding troops trained for landings from the sea, hence amphibious soldiers.

clue.text: Cigar that produces a flawless ring

parts.note: flawless means perfect
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A smoker blowing an immaculate smoke ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfecto is a type of cigar thick in the middle and tapering at both ends.

clue.text: Stroke to settle before opening of Turnberry

indicators.note: before places the settle word ahead of the next letter

parts.note: to put something is to place or settle it

indicators.note: the opening of Turnberry is the first letter of that word

explanation.surface: A golfer lines up a shot to settle matters at the start of a round at Turnberry.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnberry is a famous golf links on the Scottish coast, which sets the golfing scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A putt is a gentle golf stroke made on the green.

clue.text: Such a procurator is concerned with public revenue

explanation.surface: Describing a Scottish legal official who deals with tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A procurator fiscal is a Scottish public prosecutor; the adjective also means relating to government taxation and finances.

clue.text: I leave biscuit out for Picasso, perhaps

indicators.note: out signals the remaining letters are put out of order and rearranged
I leave tells us the letter I departs from the word biscuit

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a biscuit while looking at a Picasso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave' drops the I from BISCUIT, leaving BSCUIT, and 'out' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso founded the Cubist movement, so he is an example of a Cubist painter.

clue.text: No restriction in this Scottish resort?

parts.note: O is a nought, meaning none or no
a ban is a restriction

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Scottish town has no rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Oban is a seaside town on the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a coastal town in Argyll, popular with holidaymakers, so a Scottish resort.

clue.text: An objection intended, say, to this architectural feature

indicators.note: say signals the phrase is spoken and the sound gives the entry

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts; intended means meant

explanation.surface: Someone raises an objection to a feature of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells us A BUT MEANT spoken aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutment is a structure supporting the thrust of an arch or bridge, a building element.

clue.text: Jailbird leaves shrink and gets a stretch

indicators.note: leaves means the jailbird departs from the shrink word

parts.note: contraction is shrinking
a con is a convict, a jailbird

explanation.surface: A prisoner walks out on his psychiatrist and is given a prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' and 'stretch' look like a psychiatrist and a prison sentence; here shrink is the noun contraction and stretch is pulling.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the medical pulling of a limb to straighten it, a stretch.

clue.text: Dawn on record?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sunrise has been written down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something registers when it dawns on you, sinking into the mind; a register is also an official record or list.

clue.text: Heraldic lion spotted in Africa

explanation.surface: A heraldic lion seen on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a lion passant guardant is called a leopard; the big cat with a spotted coat roams Africa.

clue.text: Showering under dam can be exhausting

indicators.note: under places the showering word below the dam letter in this down clue

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dam, a mother animal, in pedigrees
showering means raining

explanation.surface: Water pouring down beneath a dam might wear you out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts RAINING below D.
explanation.definitionFit: Draining means using up all one's energy, so tiring or exhausting.

clue.text: Let trio go made in opera

indicators.note: made signals the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Three singers allowed to perform in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges LET TRIO GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is a Verdi opera about a court jester.

clue.text: Golden mean tend to come out embellished

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: to come out suggests the letters break out of their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Moderation tends to emerge in decorative form.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; 'to come out' rearranges MEAN TEND into NAMENTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamented means decorated with adornments, the same as embellished.

clue.text: Plum position for a railway porter?

definitions.text: Plum position for a railway porter?

parts.words: Plum position for a railway porter?
parts.note: a plum job is a fine one, but a Victoria is also a variety of plum, and a station is a position, so a porter would be posted there

explanation.surface: A railway porter landing a choice job.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a British plum variety and a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A London rail terminus named after a plum variety, where porters work, fits the porter's posting.

clue.text: Yorkshire spa town not opening? That is appropriate!

indicators.note: not opening means the town is given without its first letter

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire spa town that will not open, which seems fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' is the verb: to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate is to claim or seize without right, which is to appropriate.

clue.text: In Virginia, reds turn out to be aliens

parts.note: taken as written
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Communists in Virginia are revealed to be foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' rearranges REDS into DERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaders are hostile intruders from outside, like the aliens of science fiction.

clue.text: To give back about one shilling is called for

indicators.note: about means the give-back word goes around the next letters

parts.note: to requite is to repay or give back
I is the Roman numeral one
S was the abbreviation for a shilling, a former British coin

explanation.surface: Returning around a shilling is expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and S inside REQUITE; a shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Requisite means required or necessary, as when something is called for.

clue.text: Cowers from game birds

explanation.surface: Something shrinks back from partridges and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to flinch in fear; quails are small birds shot as game.

clue.text: Shakespeare's winter wall-hanging?

parts.note: the winter song in Love's Labour's Lost tells of frozen spikes that hang by the wall, not a tapestry

explanation.surface: A tapestry the playwright hung in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: The song begins 'When icicles hang by the wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen spike of dripping water hangs from walls and eaves in winter, as Shakespeare's song describes.

clue.text: System of radicals

parts.note: radicals look political but here they are roots, from the Latin for root, and a network of them forms a plant's underground structure

explanation.surface: A network of political extremists.
explanation.definitionFit: Rootage is the whole root system of a plant, and radical literally means of the root.

clue.text: Penchants for sloping south

parts.note: sloping means leaning

explanation.surface: A liking for land falling away to the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Leanings are inclinations or preferences, synonyms for penchants.

clue.text: Star part chosen by Bassanio

explanation.surface: The main role goes to a character in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice Bassanio wins Portia by picking the leaden casket.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead is the principal role in a show; Bassanio chooses the casket made of the grey metal.

clue.text: Long tale a sensation when brought up

indicators.note: brought up means the letters are raised from bottom to top in this down clue

parts.note: a gas is a sensation, something great fun

explanation.surface: A lengthy story that causes a stir when raised.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'when brought up' reverses A GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, often a family chronicle or Norse epic.

clue.text: Pop retires with Mum, say? That is clear

indicators.note: retires means the word goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: pa is a name for father
a mother is an example of a parent

explanation.surface: Dad steps back and leaves it to Mum, and that is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' reverses PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly visible or evident, a synonym for clear.

clue.text: Difficulty in making out in daily sex, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A frank complaint about trouble with daily intimacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making out' looks like romance but means deciphering words; 'possibly' rearranges DAILY SEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyslexia is a learning difficulty with reading, deciphering letters and words.

clue.text: Stopped losing head and relaxed

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: stopped means ceased

explanation.surface: Someone stopped and relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or calmed, which is relaxed.
